name: INT
description: INT rounds a number down to the nearest integer, toward negative infinity.
tldr: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The real number you want to round down to an integer.

basicExample.explanation: 4 is the largest integer less than or equal to 4.3.

advancedExamples.title: Negative numbers go down
advancedExamples.description: INT always moves toward negative infinity, not toward zero.
advancedExamples.explanation: The largest integer ≤ -4.3 is -5, so INT rounds away from zero for negatives.

advancedExamples.title: Extract the integer part of a division
advancedExamples.description: Combine with MOD for quotient and remainder.

howItWorks: INT returns the greatest integer that is less than or equal to the input. For positive numbers this drops the fractional part; for negatives it moves to the next lower integer. Unlike TRUNC, INT rounds toward negative infinity.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the integer result.

limitations: INT always rounds down (toward negative infinity), so INT(-4.3) = -5, which surprises users expecting -4.
For simply dropping decimals without rounding, use TRUNC instead.
Result is still a floating-point number with .0.

commonErrors.cause: INT rounds negatives down, not toward zero.
commonErrors.fix: Use TRUNC if you want to drop the sign-preserving fractional part.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: INT works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between INT and TRUNC?
faq.answer: INT rounds down toward negative infinity (INT(-4.3)=-5), while TRUNC just drops the fractional part toward zero (TRUNC(-4.3)=-4).

faq.question: How do I get just the whole-number part?
faq.answer: For positive numbers INT and TRUNC give the same result; for negatives prefer TRUNC to avoid rounding.

faq.question: Can INT return a decimal?
faq.answer: No, it always returns an integer value (stored as a number with no fractional part).
